sources.title: Н. Н. Торнау. Учебный атлас по русской истории
sources.institution: Санкт-Петербургское издание 1910 г.; цифровые копии — Wikimedia Commons / проект «Исторические Материалы»
sources.coverage: Historical cartographic reconstructions of Rus and Russia from the 9th century onward
sources.notes: Secondary late-imperial historical reconstruction. It may define the geometry of a named reconstruction layer when digitized reproducibly, but it cannot by itself establish a primary-source thin state boundary. Early-period layers must retain frontier/uncertainty semantics and cite independent primary documentary evidence for the underlying historical chronology.

sources.title: Границы России и предшественников, 850–2020
sources.institution: Руниверс / Лаборатория исторической геоинформатики Института всеобщей истории РАН / NextGIS
sources.coverage: Dynamic scholarly GIS reconstruction of political boundaries of Russia and predecessor polities from the medieval period through the modern era
sources.notes: Research cross-check only. Runivers' published site terms restrict portal materials to personal non-commercial use and prohibit commercial reuse or derivative works without prior consent. History Core therefore MUST NOT vendor, trace, transform, or derive production geometry from Runivers GIS unless separate written permission is obtained. The project remains useful for identifying historical intervals, methodology and candidate underlying sources.

sources.title: ГУГК. Учебные исторические карты Древнерусского государства IX–XI вв.
sources.institution: Главное управление геодезии и картографии; Российская государственная библиотека
sources.coverage: Kievan Rus / Old Russian state, 882–1054, including differentiated reign-period and accession layers
sources.notes: State-cartographic historical reconstruction compiled by GUGK with B. A. Rybakov as consultant; the 1961 edition is 1:3,000,000 with geographic graticule and explicitly distinguishes the Oleg 882–912 state from later 912–971 and 972–1054 accessions. It is a secondary historical reconstruction, not a contemporary medieval survey. Production geometry should be derived only after reuse rights for the raster are established or from an independently reusable source.
